newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges trade lower with little demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges trade lower with little demand.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges traded at lower numbers early on Thursday with traders saying the market was sapped by low demand, while high sulphur cargoes were offered weaker.

After early trades of high sulphur barges at $84 and $83.50 a tonne fob ARA, deals dipped to $82, or some $2 lower than Wednesday's late levels. Later sellers were said to be at $82.50 but no buying interest was seen.
"The best buyers are at $82 but demand is not too good. There were only two big inquiries only," one trader said.
Bunkers traded at a lower $85 a tonne for 380 CST material.
Low sulphur barges were quiet but traders said talk was still at a steady $95/$96. "The product is available but there's not a lot of demand," one trader said.

High sulphur cargoes seemed weaker with little demand seen and swaps talked lower at $81.50/$82 for July. One Scandinavian refiner was said to be offering his cargo at a floating price equivalent to about $77 a tonne fob. The cargo was on offer last week at $81 fob.

In the Mediterranean, a U.K-based major picked up a cargo of bunker grade high sulphur late on Wednesday from a trading house with half priced at $87 a tonne cif Gibraltar and the second half at mean cif Med plus 25 cents.
The buyer was also said to be looking for a cargo into Las Palmas and was bidding a floating price, fob Med minus $1.
Traders said three Russian M-100 cargoes were on offer at slightly lower prices than Wednesday with buyers and sellers $1 apart.

Two were straight-run offered at two means plus $1.50, or 50 cents lower than a day earlier, with buyers at two means plus 50 cents while the buy/sell range for the cracked cargo was at two means minus $2 and minus $1.
